start.text: A big bald man with a rust-red beard stands by the fire with his hands on his hips and his sleeves rolled, looking out at the fog over the sea as if it owed him money.
Boat's coming. Abe Dray. Him over there's my brother. He'll tell you it isn't.

choice.text: Why are you so sure the boat's coming?
There's a rake driven into a waymark on the old road.

sure.text: Forty years I've been the one says it won't rain, it won't hold, it won't light, and forty years Tolly's said it will. Then we come down a cliff and he's gone and took my side. So I took his. Somebody has to.
He looks at the fog over the water a while longer.
I'll tell you what, though. Hoping's harder work than a clamp. I don't know how he did it all those years.

rake.text: Ours. Mine. His. Never once agreed whose, and we had it forty years between us.

Fifth mark on the road, Tolly sat down and said he wasn't carrying it another step, and I said it wasn't his to put down. So we cut a notch across both our marks and drove it in the cairn. A rake that's both of ours is the road's.
First thing we ever agreed on.
Second. We both agreed you were wrong about the first.

home.text: Abe Dray stands across the clamp from his brother with his hands on his hips, watching Tolly hold the lantern.
Higher. You're holding it like a kettle.
The Lamp knew my face. Thirty winters, and I'd have said it never once looked at it. Said 'Abe Dray' before I'd opened my mouth, and broke a bit of its coal for us like breaking bread.
Boat never came. I'll not say I was wrong. I'll say it was late.
Hob looked at us like we were weather. Nice enough. Asked if we were for the camp. Well. We know him, if he doesn't know us. That's a start.
